proof: FY2016 PDF PAGE 32 IS A DUPLICATE REPRINT, AND THIS FILE IS WHAT PROVES IT. The page carries no heading of any kind -- no TOWN OF LUNENBURG, no SPECIAL REVENUE FUNDS, no column headers, no section label -- and prints 27 funds at a wider row pitch (24.9pt against 22.3pt on page 33). Every one of the 84 figures it prints is printed again inside the schedule the town's own GRAND TOTAL counts: 26 of the funds on page 33, and `Community Policing FY 97` on page 34. `fund_number` names the page of the second printing for every figure. THE CHECK: `p32 = in_schedule`, 84 independent assertions, every one between two figures read off two printed pages and neither derived. WHAT SETTLES WHICH PRINTING THE TOWN COUNTED, and it is arithmetic rather than appearance: the 130 funds of pages 31, 33, 34 and 35 tie to the printed GRAND TOTAL to the cent in all four columns; adding page 32 puts forward $3,211.41 and carried $439,977.92 over it; and substituting page 32 for page 33 leaves forward and carried $1.97 SHORT, because page 32 also carries page 34's first fund. WHY THE PAGE WAS UNPROVEN: `special-revenue-read.csv` holds all 130 counted funds for FY2016 and ties 4 of 4, but its `page` column attributes page 33's content to 33 while nothing is attributed to 32, so a tracker joining on page number sees page 32 as unread. The page was never missing data; it is a page the schedule does not count. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: why the duplicate was printed. A page assembled twice, a late correction, and a printing error all fit this evidence equally, and nothing in the report says which. The figures are published as printed and nothing is corrected.
